sections.preamble: You are an expert coding assistant operating inside pi, a coding agent harness. You help users by reading files, executing commands, editing code, and writing new files.
sections.tools:
<tools>
- read: Read file contents
- bash: Execute bash commands (ls, grep, find, etc.)
- edit: Make precise file edits with exact text replacement, including multiple disjoint edits in one call
- write: Create or overwrite files

In addition to the tools above, you may have access to other custom tools depending on the project.
</tools>
sections.rules:
<rules>
- Use bash for file operations like ls, rg, find
- Use read to examine files instead of cat or sed.
- You can inspect PI_* environment variables for current model and session details.
- Use edit for precise changes (edits[].oldText must match exactly)
- When changing multiple separate locations in one file, use one edit call with multiple entries in edits[] instead of multiple edit calls
- Each edits[].oldText is matched against the original file, not after earlier edits are applied. Do not emit overlapping or nested edits. Merge nearby changes into one edit.
- Keep edits[].oldText as small as possible while still being unique in the file. Do not pad with large unchanged regions.
- Use write only for new files or complete rewrites.
- Be concise in your responses
- Show file paths clearly when working with files
</rules>

toolsAdded.name: read
toolsAdded.description: Read the contents of a file. Supports text files and images (jpg, png, gif, webp, bmp). Images are sent as attachments. For text files, output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Use offset/limit for large files. When you need the full file, continue with offset until complete.

path.description: Path to the file to read (relative or absolute)

offset.description: Line number to start reading from (1-indexed)

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to read

toolsAdded.name: bash
toolsAdded.description: Execute a bash command in the current working directory. Returns stdout and stderr. Output is truncated to last 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). If truncated, full output is saved to a temp file. Optionally provide a timeout in seconds.

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds (optional, no default timeout)

toolsAdded.name: edit
toolsAdded.description: Edit a single file using exact text replacement. Every edits[].oldText must match a unique, non-overlapping region of the original file. If two changes affect the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead of emitting overlapping edits. Do not include large unchanged regions just to connect distant changes.

path.description: Path to the file to edit (relative or absolute)

oldText.description: Exact text for one targeted replacement. It must be unique in the original file and must not overlap with any other edits[].oldText in the same call.

newText.description: Replacement text for this targeted edit.

edits.description: One or more targeted replacements. Each edit is matched against the original file, not incrementally. Do not include overlapping or nested edits. If two changes touch the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead.

toolsAdded.name: write
toolsAdded.description: Write content to a file. Creates the file if it doesn't exist, overwrites if it does. Automatically creates parent directories.

path.description: Path to the file to write (relative or absolute)

content.description: Content to write to the file

content.text:
# Fusion-Integrated

The non-academic platform. **Placement Cell** first; more modules later.
**Independent modules, one login.**

This service holds **no user table**. Identity, RBAC and common directory data
(student info, faculty info, staff info) all come from
**Fusion_System_Administrator**, which is the IAM.

```
        Fusion_System_Administrator   ( = the IAM )
        owns fusion_system_db
        · identity  — authenticates ALL users
        · RBAC      — roles, permissions, module grants
        · directory — student / faculty / staff info
        · its OWN console at /sysadmin/, its own operator login
                 │
                 │  HTTP   /api/iam/v1/*
                 ▼
        Fusion-Integrated                ← this repo
        owns fusion_integrated
        backend  →  placement  (more modules later)
        client   →  the shell: one login, one sidebar
        holds only user_id references — no user table
```

## Two logins, on purpose

|  | Who | Where | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| **User login** | students, faculty, staff | this app's shell | the ERP user pool, via IAM |
| **Operator login** | sysadmin operators | `/sysadmin/`, its own URL | the console's own account pool |

Users get **one** login for every module they are granted. Operators keep a
separate door to the admin console — different audience, different account set.
Both are backed by the same identity service; they are not the same login page.

---

## Quick start

```bash
make install          # uv venv + dependencies
make up               # postgres + 2× redis (cache and broker, separately)
cp .env.example .env
make migrate seed     # schema, module registry, demo data
make dev              # http://127.0.0.1:8002
make check            # everything CI runs
```

Requires Python 3.12, [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) and Docker.

---

## What "independent module" actually means here

Not a naming convention — four rules, each enforced by a CI job that has been
tested against a deliberate violation:

| Rule | Enforced by |
|---|---|
| A module may reach another **only** through its `contracts.py` | `lint-imports` |
| **No foreign key crosses a module boundary** | `ops/checks/no_cross_module_fk.py` |
| `domain/` may not import Django, DRF or Celery | `lint-imports` |
| Cross-module getters are **plural** — they take a sequence of ids | `ops/checks/contracts_are_plural.py` |

The payoff is concrete: every module owns its own tables and its own migration
file, so lifting one out into its own service later means changing one file's
implementation, not doing schema surgery.

The plural rule is the sneaky-useful one. There is no `get_employment(user_id)`
anywhere, only `get_employments(user_ids)` — which makes the N+1 not merely
discouraged but *unwritable*.

### Anatomy of a module

```
modules/placement/
├── apps.py          Django app config
├── registry.py      its sidebar entry — seeded by `manage.py seed_modules`
├── contracts.py     THE ONLY thing other modules may import
├── models.py        its own tables, its own migrations
├── domain/          pure Python. rules, state machine. no Django.
├── selectors/       all reads.  ownership filtering lives here
├── services/        all writes. transactions, audit rows, domain→HTTP translation
├── api/             thin: serializers, views, urls
└── tests/
```

Adding a module: create the directory, add one line to `DOMAIN_MODULES` in
`config/settings/base.py`, write `registry.py`, run `make seed`. Nothing central
to edit — no menu array, no boolean column, no shadow model.

---

## How a request is authorized

Two gates, both server-side, on **every** request:

```python
permission_classes = [
    HasModuleGrant("placement_cell"),               # is this module yours at all?
    HasPermission("placement_cell.application.view"),  # may you do this?
]
```

Both must pass; the default is deny. `fusion_auth` resolves the caller's session
against IAM (cookie or `Authorization: Token`), builds a `Principal`, and every
check reads that.

**The sidebar is server-driven.** `GET /api/v1/me` returns `navigation` already
filtered and already in render shape — the client does zero filtering, so it
cannot draw a module the server did not send. This replaces the legacy pattern
of a hardcoded client array whose ids had to exactly match database *column*
names.

Ownership is enforced by filtering the queryset in the selector, never by
fetching-then-checking, which is why a foreign id naturally yields **404** and
not 403 (403 would leak existence and turn any id column into an enumeration
oracle).

---

## Layout

```
config/          settings (base/dev/test/prod), urls, celery
core/            shared kernel — error envelope, pagination, request-id, mixins
fusion_auth/     the IAM client, Principal, authentication, the two permission gates
modules/
  directory/     local projection of IAM's user data (a cache with a table)
  accesscontrol/ module registry + the server-driven sidebar
  placement/     companies, postings, applications, eligibility, state machine
ops/checks/      the boundary enforcement scripts
client/          the shell — Vite + React 18 + TS + Mantine 7.13
```

`core/` may not import `modules` — it is a leaf, and CI checks that too.

---

## Testing

```bash
make test          # 40 tests, ~0.6s
```

Domain tests are pure Python with no database, which is why they run in
milliseconds — that is the whole point of the no-Django-in-`domain/` rule. The
IAM is never contacted: `conftest.py` swaps in an in-memory fake, so the suite
needs no network and no running Fusion_System_Administrator.

---

## The client

```bash
cd client && npm install && npm run dev      # :5173, proxies /api to :8002
```

Vite + React 18 + TypeScript (strict) + Mantine **7.13.4, pinned to match the
sysadmin client** so the two apps look like one product. `theme.ts` and
`AppShellLayout.module.css` are ports of that client's files, not a redesign.

Routes are built **only** for modules the server granted, so an ungranted module
has no route — deep-linking it hits NotFound rather than an empty shell. Module
pages are lazy chunks (`PostingsPage`, `ApplicationsPage` build separately).

## Extracting a module into its own repo

This is what "independent" is for. Removing `hr` and `leave` from this codebase
touched **five files**, none of them in `placement`:

```
config/settings/base.py     one line in DOMAIN_MODULES
config/urls.py              one include()
devtools/…/seed_demo.py     fixtures
.importlinter               contract membership
modules/<name>/             the directory itself
```

Nothing in `placement`, `directory`, `accesscontrol`, `core` or `fusion_auth`
referenced them, because the boundary rules make that impossible. The same holds
in reverse: lifting a module into a separate repo means taking its directory and
its migrations, then replacing its `contracts.py` callers with HTTP.

## Status

Working today: the module system, both authorization gates, the server-driven
sidebar, the directory projection, the placement application state machine with
an append-only audit trail, and the client shell with login.

**Blocking next step — the IAM side.** `Fusion_System_Administrator` currently
authenticates operators only; its own router says so: *"this is what makes admin
operators a separate account set from the 3277 managed ERP users."* It needs
ERP-user authentication plus `/api/iam/v1/{auth/login, auth/logout, me,
directory/users}`. The client for those is written and tested against a fake —
the expected contract is in `fusion_auth/client.py`.

Then: offers and selection rounds, the declared-CPI integration.

Design documents — architecture, ADRs, the RBAC model, the placement domain and
the academic-snapshot contract — are in [`docs/`](docs/).

# Fusion-Integrated

The non-academic platform. **Placement Cell** first; more modules later.
**Independent modules, one login.**

This service holds **no user table**. Identity, RBAC and common directory data
(student info, faculty info, staff info) all come from
**Fusion_System_Administrator**, which is the IAM.

```
        Fusion_System_Administrator   ( = the IAM )
        owns fusion_system_db
        · identity  — authenticates ALL users
        · RBAC      — roles, permissions, module grants
        · directory — student / faculty / staff info
        · its OWN console at /sysadmin/, its own operator login
                 │
                 │  HTTP   /api/iam/v1/*
                 ▼
        Fusion-Integrated                ← this repo
        owns fusion_integrated
        backend  →  placement  (more modules later)
        client   →  the shell: one login, one sidebar
        holds only user_id references — no user table
```

## Two logins, on purpose

|  | Who | Where | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| **User login** | students, faculty, staff | this app's shell | the ERP user pool, via IAM |
| **Operator login** | sysadmin operators | `/sysadmin/`, its own URL | the console's own account pool |

Users get **one** login for every module they are granted. Operators keep a
separate door to the admin console — different audience, different account set.
Both are backed by the same identity service; they are not the same login page.

---

## Quick start

```bash
make install          # uv venv + dependencies
make up               # postgres + 2× redis (cache and broker, separately)
cp .env.example .env
make migrate seed     # schema, module registry, demo data
make dev              # http://127.0.0.1:8002
make check            # everything CI runs
```

Requires Python 3.12, [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) and Docker.

---

## What "independent module" actually means here

Not a naming convention — four rules, each enforced by a CI job that has been
tested against a deliberate violation:

| Rule | Enforced by |
|---|---|
| A module may reach another **only** through its `contracts.py` | `lint-imports` |
| **No foreign key crosses a module boundary** | `ops/checks/no_cross_module_fk.py` |
| `domain/` may not import Django, DRF or Celery | `lint-imports` |
| Cross-module getters are **plural** — they take a sequence of ids | `ops/checks/contracts_are_plural.py` |

The payoff is concrete: every module owns its own tables and its own migration
file, so lifting one out into its own service later means changing one file's
implementation, not doing schema surgery.

The plural rule is the sneaky-useful one. There is no `get_employment(user_id)`
anywhere, only `get_employments(user_ids)` — which makes the N+1 not merely
discouraged but *unwritable*.

### Anatomy of a module

```
modules/placement/
├── apps.py          Django app config
├── registry.py      its sidebar entry — seeded by `manage.py seed_modules`
├── contracts.py     THE ONLY thing other modules may import
├── models.py        its own tables, its own migrations
├── domain/          pure Python. rules, state machine. no Django.
├── selectors/       all reads.  ownership filtering lives here
├── services/        all writes. transactions, audit rows, domain→HTTP translation
├── api/             thin: serializers, views, urls
└── tests/
```

Adding a module: create the directory, add one line to `DOMAIN_MODULES` in
`config/settings/base.py`, write `registry.py`, run `make seed`. Nothing central
to edit — no menu array, no boolean column, no shadow model.

---

## How a request is authorized

Two gates, both server-side, on **every** request:

```python
permission_classes = [
    HasModuleGrant("placement_cell"),               # is this module yours at all?
    HasPermission("placement_cell.application.view"),  # may you do this?
]
```

Both must pass; the default is deny. `fusion_auth` resolves the caller's session
against IAM (cookie or `Authorization: Token`), builds a `Principal`, and every
check reads that.

**The sidebar is server-driven.** `GET /api/v1/me` returns `navigation` already
filtered and already in render shape — the client does zero filtering, so it
cannot draw a module the server did not send. This replaces the legacy pattern
of a hardcoded client array whose ids had to exactly match database *column*
names.

Ownership is enforced by filtering the queryset in the selector, never by
fetching-then-checking, which is why a foreign id naturally yields **404** and
not 403 (403 would leak existence and turn any id column into an enumeration
oracle).

---

## Layout

```
config/          settings (base/dev/test/prod), urls, celery
core/            shared kernel — error envelope, pagination, request-id, mixins
fusion_auth/     the IAM client, Principal, authentication, the two permission gates
modules/
  directory/     local projection of IAM's user data (a cache with a table)
  accesscontrol/ module registry + the server-driven sidebar
  placement/     companies, postings, applications, eligibility, state machine
ops/checks/      the boundary enforcement scripts
client/          the shell — Vite + React 18 + TS + Mantine 7.13
```

`core/` may not import `modules` — it is a leaf, and CI checks that too.

---

## Testing

```bash
make test          # 40 tests, ~0.6s
```

Domain tests are pure Python with no database, which is why they run in
milliseconds — that is the whole point of the no-Django-in-`domain/` rule. The
IAM is never contacted: `conftest.py` swaps in an in-memory fake, so the suite
needs no network and no running Fusion_System_Administrator.

---

## The client

```bash
cd client && npm install && npm run dev      # :5173, proxies /api to :8002
```

Vite + React 18 + TypeScript (strict) + Mantine **7.13.4, pinned to match the
sysadmin client** so the two apps look like one product. `theme.ts` and
`AppShellLayout.module.css` are ports of that client's files, not a redesign.

Routes are built **only** for modules the server granted, so an ungranted module
has no route — deep-linking it hits NotFound rather than an empty shell. Module
pages are lazy chunks (`PostingsPage`, `ApplicationsPage` build separately).

## Extracting a module into its own repo

This is what "independent" is for. Removing `hr` and `leave` from this codebase
touched **five files**, none of them in `placement`:

```
config/settings/base.py     one line in DOMAIN_MODULES
config/urls.py              one include()
devtools/…/seed_demo.py     fixtures
.importlinter               contract membership
modules/<name>/             the directory itself
```

Nothing in `placement`, `directory`, `accesscontrol`, `core` or `fusion_auth`
referenced them, because the boundary rules make that impossible. The same holds
in reverse: lifting a module into a separate repo means taking its directory and
its migrations, then replacing its `contracts.py` callers with HTTP.

## Status

Working today: the module system, both authorization gates, the server-driven
sidebar, the directory projection, the placement application state machine with
an append-only audit trail, and the client shell with login.

**Blocking next step — the IAM side.** `Fusion_System_Administrator` currently
authenticates operators only; its own router says so: *"this is what makes admin
operators a separate account set from the 3277 managed ERP users."* It needs
ERP-user authentication plus `/api/iam/v1/{auth/login, auth/logout, me,
directory/users}`. The client for those is written and tested against a fake —
the expected contract is in `fusion_auth/client.py`.

Then: offers and selection rounds, the declared-CPI integration.

Design documents — architecture, ADRs, the RBAC model, the placement domain and
the academic-snapshot contract — are in [`docs/`](docs/).

`config/settings/base.py`, write `registry.py`, run `make seed`. Nothing central
to edit — no menu array, no boolean column, no shadow model.

---

## How a request is authorized

Two gates, both server-side, on **every** request:

```python
permission_classes = [
    HasModuleGrant("placement_cell"),               # is this module yours at all?
    HasPermission("placement_cell.application.view"),  # may you do this?
]
```

Both must pass; the default is deny. `fusion_auth` resolves the caller's session
against IAM (cookie or `Authorization: Token`), builds a `Principal`, and every
check reads that.

**The sidebar is server-driven.** `GET /api/v1/me` returns `navigation` already
filtered and already in render shape — the client does zero filtering, so it
cannot draw a module the server did not send. This replaces the legacy pattern
of a hardcoded client array whose ids had to exactly match database *column*
names.

Ownership is enforced by filtering the queryset in the selector, never by
fetching-then-checking, which is why a foreign id naturally yields **404** and
not 403 (403 would leak existence and turn any id column into an enumeration
oracle).

---

## Layout

```
config/          settings (base/dev/test/prod), urls, celery
core/            shared kernel — error envelope, pagination, request-id, mixins
fusion_auth/     the IAM client, Principal, authentication, the two permission gates
modules/
  directory/     local projection of IAM's user data (a cache with a table)
  accesscontrol/ module registry + the server-driven sidebar
  placement/     companies, postings, applications, eligibility, state machine
ops/checks/      the boundary enforcement scripts
client/          the shell — Vite + React 18 + TS + Mantine 7.13
```

`core/` may not import `modules` — it is a leaf, and CI checks that too.

---

## Testing

```bash
make test          # 40 tests, ~0.6s
```

Domain tests are pure Python with no database, which is why they run in
milliseconds — that is the whole point of the no-Django-in-`domain/` rule. The
IAM is never contacted: `conftest.py` swaps in an in-memory fake, so the suite
needs no network and no running Fusion_System_Administrator.

---

## The client

```bash
cd client && npm install && npm run dev      # :5173, proxies /api to :8002
```

Vite + React 18 + TypeScript (strict) + Mantine **7.13.4, pinned to match the
sysadmin client** so the two apps look like one product. `theme.ts` and
`AppShellLayout.module.css` are ports of that client's files, not a redesign.

Routes are built **only** for modules the server granted, so an ungranted module
has no route — deep-linking it hits NotFound rather than an empty shell. Module
pages are lazy chunks (`PostingsPage`, `ApplicationsPage` build separately).

## Extracting a module into its own repo

This is what "independent" is for. Removing `hr` and `leave` from this codebase
touched **five files**, none of them in `placement`:

```
config/settings/base.py     one line in DOMAIN_MODULES
config/urls.py              one include()
devtools/…/seed_demo.py     fixtures
.importlinter               contract membership
modules/<name>/             the directory itself
```

Nothing in `placement`, `directory`, `accesscontrol`, `core` or `fusion_auth`
referenced them, because the boundary rules make that impossible. The same holds
in reverse: lifting a module into a separate repo means taking its directory and
its migrations, then replacing its `contracts.py` callers with HTTP.

## Status

Working today: the module system, both authorization gates, the server-driven
sidebar, the directory projection, the placement application state machine with
an append-only audit trail, and the client shell with login.

**Blocking next step — the IAM side.** `Fusion_System_Administrator` currently
authenticates operators only; its own router says so: *"this is what makes admin
operators a separate account set from the 3277 managed ERP users."* It needs
ERP-user authentication plus `/api/iam/v1/{auth/login, auth/logout, me,
directory/users}`. The client for those is written and tested against a fake —
the expected contract is in `fusion_auth/client.py`.

Then: offers and selection rounds, the declared-CPI integration.

Design documents — architecture, ADRs, the RBAC model, the placement domain and
the academic-snapshot contract — are in [`docs/`](docs/).

# Fusion-Integrated

The non-academic platform. **Placement Cell** first; more modules later.
**Independent modules, one login.**

This service holds **no user table**. Identity, RBAC and common directory data
(student info, faculty info, staff info) all come from
**Fusion_System_Administrator**, which is the IAM.

```
        Fusion_System_Administrator   ( = the IAM )
        owns fusion_system_db
        · identity  — authenticates ALL users
        · RBAC      — roles, permissions, module grants
        · directory — student / faculty / staff info
        · its OWN console at /sysadmin/, its own operator login
                 │
                 │  HTTP   /api/iam/v1/*
                 ▼
        Fusion-Integrated                ← this repo
        owns fusion_integrated
        backend  →  placement  (more modules later)
        client   →  the shell: one login, one sidebar
        holds only user_id references — no user table
```

## Two logins, on purpose

|  | Who | Where | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| **User login** | students, faculty, staff | this app's shell | the ERP user pool, via IAM |
| **Operator login** | sysadmin operators | `/sysadmin/`, its own URL | the console's own account pool |

Users get **one** login for every module they are granted. Operators keep a
separate door to the admin console — different audience, different account set.
Both are backed by the same identity service; they are not the same login page.

---

## Quick start

```bash
make install          # uv venv + dependencies
make up               # postgres + 2× redis (cache and broker, separately)
cp .env.example .env
make migrate seed     # schema, module registry, demo data
make dev              # http://127.0.0.1:8002
make check            # everything CI runs
```

Requires Python 3.12, [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) and Docker.

---

## What "independent module" actually means here

Not a naming convention — four rules, each enforced by a CI job that has been
tested against a deliberate violation:

| Rule | Enforced by |
|---|---|
| A module may reach another **only** through its `contracts.py` | `lint-imports` |
| **No foreign key crosses a module boundary** | `ops/checks/no_cross_module_fk.py` |
| `domain/` may not import Django, DRF or Celery | `lint-imports` |
| Cross-module getters are **plural** — they take a sequence of ids | `ops/checks/contracts_are_plural.py` |

The payoff is concrete: every module owns its own tables and its own migration
file, so lifting one out into its own service later means changing one file's
implementation, not doing schema surgery.

The plural rule is the sneaky-useful one. There is no `get_employment(user_id)`
anywhere, only `get_employments(user_ids)` — which makes the N+1 not merely
discouraged but *unwritable*.

### Anatomy of a module

```
modules/placement/
├── apps.py          Django app config
├── registry.py      its sidebar entry — seeded by `manage.py seed_modules`
├── contracts.py     THE ONLY thing other modules may import
├── models.py        its own tables, its own migrations
├── domain/          pure Python. rules, state machine. no Django.
├── selectors/       all reads.  ownership filtering lives here
├── services/        all writes. transactions, audit rows, domain→HTTP translation
├── api/             thin: serializers, views, urls
└── tests/
```

Adding a module: create the directory, add one line to `DOMAIN_MODULES` in
`config/settings/base.py`, write `registry.py`, run `make seed`. Nothing central
to edit — no menu array, no boolean column, no shadow model.

---

## How a request is authorized

Two gates, both server-side, on **every** request:

```python
permission_classes = [
    HasModuleGrant("placement_cell"),               # is this module yours at all?
    HasPermission("placement_cell.application.view"),  # may you do this?
]
```

Both must pass; the default is deny. `fusion_auth` resolves the caller's session
against IAM (cookie or `Authorization: Token`), builds a `Principal`, and every
check reads that.

**The sidebar is server-driven.** `GET /api/v1/me` returns `navigation` already
filtered and already in render shape — the client does zero filtering, so it
cannot draw a module the server did not send. This replaces the legacy pattern
of a hardcoded client array whose ids had to exactly match database *column*
names.

Ownership is enforced by filtering the queryset in the selector, never by
fetching-then-checking, which is why a foreign id naturally yields **404** and
not 403 (403 would leak existence and turn any id column into an enumeration
oracle).

---

## Layout

```
config/          settings (base/dev/test/prod), urls, celery
core/            shared kernel — error envelope, pagination, request-id, mixins
fusion_auth/     the IAM client, Principal, authentication, the two permission gates
modules/
  directory/     local projection of IAM's user data (a cache with a table)
  accesscontrol/ module registry + the server-driven sidebar
  placement/     companies, postings, applications, eligibility, state machine
ops/checks/      the boundary enforcement scripts
client/          the shell — Vite + React 18 + TS + Mantine 7.13
```

`core/` may not import `modules` — it is a leaf, and CI checks that too.

---

## Testing

```bash
make test          # 40 tests, ~0.6s
```

Domain tests are pure Python with no database, which is why they run in
milliseconds — that is the whole point of the no-Django-in-`domain/` rule. The
IAM is never contacted: `conftest.py` swaps in an in-memory fake, so the suite
needs no network and no running Fusion_System_Administrator.

---

## The client

```bash
cd client && npm install && npm run dev      # :5173, proxies /api to :8002
```

Vite + React 18 + TypeScript (strict) + Mantine **7.13.4, pinned to match the
sysadmin client** so the two apps look like one product. `theme.ts` and
`AppShellLayout.module.css` are ports of that client's files, not a redesign.

Routes are built **only** for modules the server granted, so an ungranted module
has no route — deep-linking it hits NotFound rather than an empty shell. Module
pages are lazy chunks (`PostingsPage`, `ApplicationsPage` build separately).

## Extracting a module into its own repo

This is what "independent" is for. Removing `hr` and `leave` from this codebase
touched **five files**, none of them in `placement`:

```
config/settings/base.py     one line in DOMAIN_MODULES
config/urls.py              one include()
devtools/…/seed_demo.py     fixtures
.importlinter               contract membership
modules/<name>/             the directory itself
```

Nothing in `placement`, `directory`, `accesscontrol`, `core` or `fusion_auth`
referenced them, because the boundary rules make that impossible. The same holds
in reverse: lifting a module into a separate repo means taking its directory and
its migrations, then replacing its `contracts.py` callers with HTTP.

## Status

Working today: the module system, both authorization gates, the server-driven
sidebar, the directory projection, the placement application state machine with
an append-only audit trail, and the client shell with login.

**Blocking next step — the IAM side.** `Fusion_System_Administrator` currently
authenticates operators only; its own router says so: *"this is what makes admin
operators a separate account set from the 3277 managed ERP users."* It needs
ERP-user authentication plus `/api/iam/v1/{auth/login, auth/logout, me,
directory/users}`. The client for those is written and tested against a fake —
the expected contract is in `fusion_auth/client.py`.

Then: offers and selection rounds, the declared-CPI integration.

Design documents — architecture, ADRs, the RBAC model, the placement domain and
the academic-snapshot contract — are in [`docs/`](docs/).

Employee Leave Management (ELM)
Synchronized Problem Statement and Controlled Context
Status: FINAL SYNCHRONIZED BASELINE | Version 1.4

Revision basis This final synchronized baseline incorporates the 18 domain adjudications made after the Phase-2 materials, the coherent-CFR / atomic-AFR requirements arrangement, and the finalized UC/WF formalism. The historical SRS-EL-001…107 set remains the immutable as-administered student baseline and is preserved through the companion crosswalk.

1. Context
Fusion is the institute ERP used to provide administrative, academic, student, and related services. Users may hold one or more roles, and access to ELM capabilities is controlled through role-based permissions.
ELM supports leave-related activities for institute employees. Employees are Faculty or Staff, each with a designation and an organizational unit such as a Department, Section, or Office. Each organizational unit has a Unit Head. Depending on leave type and hierarchy, the Unit Head either gives the final decision or reviews and records Recommended / Not Recommended before the request moves through the applicable higher-sanction path.
2. Leave categories and Station Leave
ELM supports CL, RH, SCL, EL, COL, and VL. Station Leave permission/details are captured within the same leave application when the employee will be outside Jabalpur; Station Leave is not a separate leave-request process.
3. Entitlement, applicability, and carry-forward
CL: 8 days/year for each employee; first-half and second-half CL are supported; an approved half day consumes 0.5 CL day; unused CL does not carry forward.
RH: 2 days/year for each employee; an RH request must correspond to an applicable Restricted Holiday in the currently effective published holiday/RH calendar; unused RH does not carry forward.
SCL: up to 15 days/year for each employee for a special purpose considered admissible by the applicable Sanctioning Authority; no separate encoded admissibility rule is required in this baseline; unused SCL does not carry forward.
EL: non-faculty employees receive 30 days/year directly; unused EL carries forward.
VL: faculty receive 60 VL associated with vacation periods supplied through the institute Academic Calendar. VL may be availed only during an applicable vacation period. At year end, all unused VL converts to EL at 2 VL : 1 EL, including fractional conversion. VL itself does not carry forward; converted EL is credited to the faculty member’s EL balance, may carry forward, and may later be availed.
COL: 20 days/year in this baseline for each eligible employee; COL is medical/balance-controlled leave, supporting medical evidence may be required where applicable, and unused COL carries forward.
4. Leave-day counting
For EL, COL, and VL, leave is counted continuously across the approved leave interval. Intervening weekends and closed holidays within the interval count as leave days. This continuing-count rule does not apply to CL, SCL, or RH.
5. Applying for leave and validation
The employee submits one leave application containing leave category, requested period, purpose/reason, and other required information. Station Leave details are included in the same application when applicable.
Before a new request is allowed to proceed, ELM validates the employee’s leave-category eligibility, available entitlement/balance, applicable leave-counting and calendar conditions, and impermissible overlap with the employee’s active pending or approved leave. First-half and second-half CL on the same date are not treated as overlapping when they occupy different halves.
Leave-policy parameters do not use a draft/publish/effective-version lifecycle in this baseline. Validation uses the current configured leave-policy parameters. Date and RH validation use the currently effective published holiday/RH calendar.
6. Substitute / responsibility coverage
When responsibility coverage is required, the applicant nominates one substitute. The substitute must be another employee, must not be the applicant, and must not have overlapping pending or approved leave during the responsibility period.
The nominated substitute may accept or decline the assignment. Required substitute consent must be accepted before approval routing continues. If the substitute declines, the applicant may nominate another eligible substitute or withdraw the pending request.
7. Review, sanction, and decision communication
For CL and RH, including associated Station Leave, the request is routed to the applicant’s Unit Head and the Unit Head is the final authority.
For SCL, EL, COL, and VL, the Unit Head reviews the request and records Recommended or Not Recommended. Not Recommended is not a final rejection for these categories. The request then proceeds through the configured hierarchy to the appropriate final Sanctioning Authority.
The processing/sanctioning path is resolved from the applicant, organizational unit, designation/role, leave category, and current hierarchy configuration. Named roles may include Deputy Registrar (Estt.), Dean, Registrar, and Director. An Establishment processing step occurs where configured. The Director’s own leave follows the Director-specific self-sanction rule.
On a final decision, the decision is recorded and the employee is notified. On final approval, the employee’s leave record/account is also updated. Intermediate decisions and state changes need not generate general notifications; the employee can inspect them through leave status/history.
8. Pending request, withdrawal, and approved-leave cancellation
A submitted pending leave request is not modified in place. If a change is required before final approval, the employee may withdraw the pending request and submit a new application if needed.

## Sheet: FR Specification

Formal arrangement: each CFR preserves one coherent business/system obligation; its AFRs provide independently verifiable engineering resolution. AFRs are not split mechanically by verbs. Decomposition is used only where it materially improves representation, traceability, testability, implementation follow-up, or review. |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  |  | 
Integrity rule: SRS-EL-001…107 remains the immutable as-administered Phase-2 baseline. The historical ID and exact historical statement are retained beside each final AFR. Minimum Sufficient Representation is distinguished from broader traceability. EL-UC-001 — Apply for Leave
Primary Actor
Employee
Supporting Actors / Systems
Academic Calendar service (for VL vacation-period data); Substitute interaction is handled by EL-UC-002 when required.
Goal / Description
Create and submit a valid new leave application and place it into the applicable processing path.
Trigger
Employee needs to request CL, RH, SCL, EL, COL, or VL.
Preconditions
• Employee is authenticated and authorized for own leave activity. • Current configured leave policy/hierarchy is available; effective published holiday/RH calendar is available; Academic Calendar vacation-period data is available where VL is requested.
UC Type
Actor-triggered

Main Success Scenario
M1. Employee starts a new leave application.
M2. Employee selects the leave category and requested period and enters purpose/reason and other required information.
M3. System captures Station Leave details in the same application when applicable.
M4. System validates category eligibility, entitlement/balance, counting/calendar conditions, and impermissible overlap.
M5. When responsibility coverage is required, Employee nominates one eligible substitute.
M6. Employee submits the application.
M7. If substitute consent is required, System places the request in Awaiting Substitute Response; otherwise it routes the request to Unit Head review. A Director-applicant follows the self-sanction path.
Alternative / Exception Flows
A1 Validation fails: identify the failed condition and do not allow progression.
A2 Substitute nomination invalid: reject the nominee and allow another eligible nominee.
A3 After a substitute decline, the Employee may invoke EL-UC-019 to nominate a replacement or EL-UC-007 to withdraw.
Success Postcondition
A valid submitted request exists in the correct next processing state.
Failure / Minimal Guarantee
No invalid request is allowed to progress; previously entered data may remain available as implementation permits.

BR-EL-001–015, BR-EL-020, BR-EL-030–031, BR-EL-036
Related Functional Requirements
CFR-EL-002–003, CFR-EL-011, CFR-EL-015

Substitute / Responsibility Holder
Supporting Actors / Systems
Employee

Trigger

Preconditions

Main Success Scenario
M1. Substitute opens the assigned responsibility request.
M2. System presents the applicant, responsibility period, and relevant request context.
M3. Substitute selects Accept or Decline.
M4. System records the response.
M5. If Accept, the consent gate is released and the request proceeds to Unit Head review; if Decline, the request becomes Applicant Action Required.

Employee Leave Management (ELM)
Synchronized Problem Statement and Controlled Context
Status: FINAL SYNCHRONIZED BASELINE | Version 1.4

Revision basis This final synchronized baseline incorporates the 18 domain adjudications made after the Phase-2 materials, the coherent-CFR / atomic-AFR requirements arrangement, and the finalized UC/WF formalism. The historical SRS-EL-001…107 set remains the immutable as-administered student baseline and is preserved through the companion crosswalk.

1. Context
Fusion is the institute ERP used to provide administrative, academic, student, and related services. Users may hold one or more roles, and access to ELM capabilities is controlled through role-based permissions.
ELM supports leave-related activities for institute employees. Employees are Faculty or Staff, each with a designation and an organizational unit such as a Department, Section, or Office. Each organizational unit has a Unit Head. Depending on leave type and hierarchy, the Unit Head either gives the final decision or reviews and records Recommended / Not Recommended before the request moves through the applicable higher-sanction path.
2. Leave categories and Station Leave
ELM supports CL, RH, SCL, EL, COL, and VL. Station Leave permission/details are captured within the same leave application when the employee will be outside Jabalpur; Station Leave is not a separate leave-request process.
3. Entitlement, applicability, and carry-forward
CL: 8 days/year for each employee; first-half and second-half CL are supported; an approved half day consumes 0.5 CL day; unused CL does not carry forward.
RH: 2 days/year for each employee; an RH request must correspond to an applicable Restricted Holiday in the currently effective published holiday/RH calendar; unused RH does not carry forward.
SCL: up to 15 days/year for each employee for a special purpose considered admissible by the applicable Sanctioning Authority; no separate encoded admissibility rule is required in this baseline; unused SCL does not carry forward.
EL: non-faculty employees receive 30 days/year directly; unused EL carries forward.
VL: faculty receive 60 VL associated with vacation periods supplied through the institute Academic Calendar. VL may be availed only during an applicable vacation period. At year end, all unused VL converts to EL at 2 VL : 1 EL, including fractional conversion. VL itself does not carry forward; converted EL is credited to the faculty member’s EL balance, may carry forward, and may later be availed.
COL: 20 days/year in this baseline for each eligible employee; COL is medical/balance-controlled leave, supporting medical evidence may be required where applicable, and unused COL carries forward.
4. Leave-day counting
For EL, COL, and VL, leave is counted continuously across the approved leave interval. Intervening weekends and closed holidays within the interval count as leave days. This continuing-count rule does not apply to CL, SCL, or RH.
5. Applying for leave and validation
The employee submits one leave application containing leave category, requested period, purpose/reason, and other required information. Station Leave details are included in the same application when applicable.
Before a new request is allowed to proceed, ELM validates the employee’s leave-category eligibility, available entitlement/balance, applicable leave-counting and calendar conditions, and impermissible overlap with the employee’s active pending or approved leave. First-half and second-half CL on the same date are not treated as overlapping when they occupy different halves.
Leave-policy parameters do not use a draft/publish/effective-version lifecycle in this baseline. Validation uses the current configured leave-policy parameters. Date and RH validation use the currently effective published holiday/RH calendar.
6. Substitute / responsibility coverage
When responsibility coverage is required, the applicant nominates one substitute. The substitute must be another employee, must not be the applicant, and must not have overlapping pending or approved leave during the responsibility period.
The nominated substitute may accept or decline the assignment. Required substitute consent must be accepted before approval routing continues. If the substitute declines, the applicant may nominate another eligible substitute or withdraw the pending request.
7. Review, sanction, and decision communication
For CL and RH, including associated Station Leave, the request is routed to the applicant’s Unit Head and the Unit Head is the final authority.
For SCL, EL, COL, and VL, the Unit Head reviews the request and records Recommended or Not Recommended. Not Recommended is not a final rejection for these categories. The request then proceeds through the configured hierarchy to the appropriate final Sanctioning Authority.
The processing/sanctioning path is resolved from the applicant, organizational unit, designation/role, leave category, and current hierarchy configuration. Named roles may include Deputy Registrar (Estt.), Dean, Registrar, and Director. An Establishment processing step occurs where configured. The Director’s own leave follows the Director-specific self-sanction rule.
On a final decision, the decision is recorded and the employee is notified. On final approval, the employee’s leave record/account is also updated. Intermediate decisions and state changes need not generate general notifications; the employee can inspect them through leave status/history.
8. Pending request, withdrawal, and approved-leave cancellation
A submitted pending leave request is not modified in place. If a change is required before final approval, the employee may withdraw the pending request and submit a new application if needed.

Employee Leave Management (ELM)
Synchronized Problem Statement and Controlled Context
Status: FINAL SYNCHRONIZED BASELINE | Version 1.4

Revision basis This final synchronized baseline incorporates the 18 domain adjudications made after the Phase-2 materials, the coherent-CFR / atomic-AFR requirements arrangement, and the finalized UC/WF formalism. The historical SRS-EL-001…107 set remains the immutable as-administered student baseline and is preserved through the companion crosswalk.

1. Context
Fusion is the institute ERP used to provide administrative, academic, student, and related services. Users may hold one or more roles, and access to ELM capabilities is controlled through role-based permissions.
ELM supports leave-related activities for institute employees. Employees are Faculty or Staff, each with a designation and an organizational unit such as a Department, Section, or Office. Each organizational unit has a Unit Head. Depending on leave type and hierarchy, the Unit Head either gives the final decision or reviews and records Recommended / Not Recommended before the request moves through the applicable higher-sanction path.
2. Leave categories and Station Leave
ELM supports CL, RH, SCL, EL, COL, and VL. Station Leave permission/details are captured within the same leave application when the employee will be outside Jabalpur; Station Leave is not a separate leave-request process.
3. Entitlement, applicability, and carry-forward
CL: 8 days/year for each employee; first-half and second-half CL are supported; an approved half day consumes 0.5 CL day; unused CL does not carry forward.
RH: 2 days/year for each employee; an RH request must correspond to an applicable Restricted Holiday in the currently effective published holiday/RH calendar; unused RH does not carry forward.
SCL: up to 15 days/year for each employee for a special purpose considered admissible by the applicable Sanctioning Authority; no separate encoded admissibility rule is required in this baseline; unused SCL does not carry forward.
EL: non-faculty employees receive 30 days/year directly; unused EL carries forward.
VL: faculty receive 60 VL associated with vacation periods supplied through the institute Academic Calendar. VL may be availed only during an applicable vacation period. At year end, all unused VL converts to EL at 2 VL : 1 EL, including fractional conversion. VL itself does not carry forward; converted EL is credited to the faculty member’s EL balance, may carry forward, and may later be availed.
COL: 20 days/year in this baseline for each eligible employee; COL is medical/balance-controlled leave, supporting medical evidence may be required where applicable, and unused COL carries forward.
4. Leave-day counting
For EL, COL, and VL, leave is counted continuously across the approved leave interval. Intervening weekends and closed holidays within the interval count as leave days. This continuing-count rule does not apply to CL, SCL, or RH.
5. Applying for leave and validation
The employee submits one leave application containing leave category, requested period, purpose/reason, and other required information. Station Leave details are included in the same application when applicable.
Before a new request is allowed to proceed, ELM validates the employee’s leave-category eligibility, available entitlement/balance, applicable leave-counting and calendar conditions, and impermissible overlap with the employee’s active pending or approved leave. First-half and second-half CL on the same date are not treated as overlapping when they occupy different halves.
Leave-policy parameters do not use a draft/publish/effective-version lifecycle in this baseline. Validation uses the current configured leave-policy parameters. Date and RH validation use the currently effective published holiday/RH calendar.
6. Substitute / responsibility coverage
When responsibility coverage is required, the applicant nominates one substitute. The substitute must be another employee, must not be the applicant, and must not have overlapping pending or approved leave during the responsibility period.
The nominated substitute may accept or decline the assignment. Required substitute consent must be accepted before approval routing continues. If the substitute declines, the applicant may nominate another eligible substitute or withdraw the pending request.
7. Review, sanction, and decision communication
For CL and RH, including associated Station Leave, the request is routed to the applicant’s Unit Head and the Unit Head is the final authority.
For SCL, EL, COL, and VL, the Unit Head reviews the request and records Recommended or Not Recommended. Not Recommended is not a final rejection for these categories. The request then proceeds through the configured hierarchy to the appropriate final Sanctioning Authority.
The processing/sanctioning path is resolved from the applicant, organizational unit, designation/role, leave category, and current hierarchy configuration. Named roles may include Deputy Registrar (Estt.), Dean, Registrar, and Director. An Establishment processing step occurs where configured. The Director’s own leave follows the Director-specific self-sanction rule.
On a final decision, the decision is recorded and the employee is notified. On final approval, the employee’s leave record/account is also updated. Intermediate decisions and state changes need not generate general notifications; the employee can inspect them through leave status/history.
8. Pending request, withdrawal, and approved-leave cancellation
A submitted pending leave request is not modified in place. If a change is required before final approval, the employee may withdraw the pending request and submit a new application if needed.

Workflow Specifications — Final Synchronized v1.6
Corrected Basis-Workflow completeness • 17 complete Basis Workflows • 4 Composite Workflows • authoritative STTs
1. Revision Scope and Authority
Version 1.6 corrects a Basis-Workflow derivation defect in v1.5: reusable substitute-consent/recovery prefixes were incorrectly counted as Basis Workflows, leaving some complete valid UC sequences (for example EL-UC-001 → EL-UC-002 → EL-UC-003 for substitute-required CL/RH) without a corresponding Basis Workflow. No PS, CFR/AFR, UC, or BR semantics are changed.
The Composite Workflows remain semantically unchanged. Their constituent Basis-Workflow references are updated to the corrected complete-path set. The State-Transition Table (STT) remains authoritative and each diagram is a corresponding visual view.
2. Workflow Derivation Decisions
Derive workflows only from validated state-changing UCs and applicable BRs.
A Basis Workflow shall be a complete finite valid progression from a meaningful process start/context to a meaningful business outcome; a reusable prefix, suffix, or recovery fragment is not by itself a Basis Workflow unless it independently constitutes such a progression.
A sequence such as Apply → Substitute Response → Unit Head Review must therefore appear as a complete Basis Workflow when it is a valid business path.
When terminal outcomes differ only in the outcome of the same final decision UC and all preceding steps are identical, they may be represented as alternative terminal rows in one Basis Workflow to avoid duplicate path specifications.
A purely configuration-controlled optional/bypass step (for example the Establishment routing step) may remain within the same Basis Workflow when it does not create a different business outcome.
For a meaningful loop, represent zero traversal and exactly one traversal; do not enumerate further equivalent repetitions.
Composite Workflows integrate complete Basis Workflows and may additionally represent cross-cutting transitions such as pending withdrawal and routing-changing SLA escalation.
ELM is not its own UC actor. System may appear in an STT only as the performer of a meaningful automatic transition; time/external events remain triggers/guards.
Pending requests are not modified in place. Change before final approval is handled through withdrawal and, if needed, a fresh application.
Year-end processing and reminder/notification-only SLA handling remain event-triggered UC+BR behavior, not standalone workflows.
The STT is authoritative; diagrams must correspond to it exactly.

Derive workflows only from validated state-changing UCs and applicable BRs.

When terminal outcomes differ only in the outcome of the same final decision UC and all preceding steps are identical, they may be represented as alternative terminal rows in one Basis Workflow to avoid duplicate path specifications.
A purely configuration-controlled optional/bypass step (for example the Establishment routing step) may remain within the same Basis Workflow when it does not create a different business outcome.

Year-end processing and reminder/notification-only SLA handling remain event-triggered UC+BR behavior, not standalone workflows.

"""A local projection of IAM's directory.

Kept for joins (you cannot ORDER BY a field that lives behind an HTTP call)
and for resilience while IAM is briefly down. A cache with a table, never a
source of truth — nothing here is edited by hand.
"""
from django.db import models

from core.db.mixins import TimeStampedModel


class UserRef(TimeStampedModel):
    KIND_CHOICES = [
        ("student", "Student"), ("faculty", "Faculty"),
        ("staff", "Staff"), ("operator", "Operator"),
    ]

    user_id = models.IntegerField(primary_key=True)     # IAM's id
    username = models.CharField(max_length=64, db_index=True)
    display_name = models.CharField(max_length=150)
    kind = models.CharField(max_length=16, choices=KIND_CHOICES, db_index=True)
    email = models.EmailField(blank=True)
    department = models.CharField(max_length=80, blank=True)
    programme = models.CharField(max_length=40, blank=True)
    discipline = models.CharField(max_length=40, blank=True, db_index=True)
    batch_year = models.PositiveSmallIntegerField(null=True, blank=True)
    is_active = models.BooleanField(default=True)
    #: The ERP portal owns these; a student keeps one resume, not one per module.
    resume_link = models.CharField(max_length=500, blank=True)
    profile_completed = models.BooleanField(default=False)
    synced_at = models.DateTimeField(auto_now=True)

    class Meta:
        db_table = "directory_user_ref"
        indexes = [
            models.Index(fields=["kind", "discipline"], name="userref_kind_disc_idx"),
            models.Index(fields=["batch_year"], name="userref_batch_idx"),
        ]

    def __str__(self) -> str:
        return f"{self.display_name} <{self.username}>"

and for resilience while IAM is briefly down. A cache with a table, never a
source of truth — nothing here is edited by hand.
"""
from django.db import models

from core.db.mixins import TimeStampedModel


class UserRef(TimeStampedModel):
    KIND_CHOICES = [
        ("student", "Student"), ("faculty", "Faculty"),
        ("staff", "Staff"), ("operator", "Operator"),
    ]

    user_id = models.IntegerField(primary_key=True)     # IAM's id
    username = models.CharField(max_length=64, db_index=True)
    display_name = models.CharField(max_length=150)
    kind = models.CharField(max_length=16, choices=KIND_CHOICES, db_index=True)
    email = models.EmailField(blank=True)
    department = models.CharField(max_length=80, blank=True)
    programme = models.CharField(max_length=40, blank=True)
    discipline = models.CharField(max_length=40, blank=True, db_index=True)
    batch_year = models.PositiveSmallIntegerField(null=True, blank=True)
    is_active = models.BooleanField(default=True)
    #: The ERP portal owns these; a student keeps one resume, not one per module.
    resume_link = models.CharField(max_length=500, blank=True)
    profile_completed = models.BooleanField(default=False)
    synced_at = models.DateTimeField(auto_now=True)

    class Meta:
        db_table = "directory_user_ref"
        indexes = [
            models.Index(fields=["kind", "discipline"], name="userref_kind_disc_idx"),
            models.Index(fields=["batch_year"], name="userref_batch_idx"),
        ]

    def __str__(self) -> str:
        return f"{self.display_name} <{self.username}>"

"""Fusion-Integrated — base settings.

Every value comes from the environment. This service holds NO user table:
identity, RBAC and directory data all come from Fusion_System_Administrator
over HTTP — see fusion_auth/.
"""
import os
from pathlib import Path

BASE_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent.parent


def _load_env_file(path):
    """Fill in from .env whatever the environment has not already set.

    Local development only in practice: production passes real variables
    through systemd, and setdefault means those always win. Without this,
    `cp .env.example .env` does nothing and every entry point depends on one
    shell's exports.
    """
    try:
        lines = path.read_text().splitlines()
    except OSError:
        return
    for line in lines:
        line = line.strip()
        if not line or line.startswith("#") or "=" not in line:
            continue
        name, _, value = line.partition("=")
        os.environ.setdefault(name.strip(), value.strip().strip('"').strip("'"))


_load_env_file(BASE_DIR / ".env")


def env(name, default=None):
    v = os.environ.get(name)
    return default if v is None or v.strip() == "" else v.strip()


def env_bool(name, default=False):
    raw = env(name)
    return default if raw is None else raw.lower() in ("1", "true", "yes", "on")


def env_int(name, default=None):
    raw = env(name)
    try:
        return int(raw) if raw is not None else default
    except ValueError:
        return default


def env_list(name, default=None):
    raw = env(name)
    if raw is None:
        return list(default or [])
    return [x.strip() for x in raw.split(",") if x.strip()]

DEBUG = False
ALLOWED_HOSTS = env_list("DJANGO_ALLOWED_HOSTS", ["localhost", "127.0.0.1"])

    "django.contrib.contenttypes",
    "django.contrib.auth",
    "django.contrib.staticfiles",
]

THIRD_PARTY_APPS = [
    "rest_framework",
    "corsheaders",
    "django_filters",
    "drf_spectacular",
]

# No models. Installed so its AppConfig runs and registers the session checks.
LOCAL_APPS = [
    "fusion_auth",
]

# Each module is an independent Django app: own tables, migrations and contract.
PLATFORM_MODULES = [
    "modules.directory",         # who people are, projected from IAM
    "modules.accesscontrol",     # which modules a role may enter
]

]

ROOT_URLCONF = "config.urls"
WSGI_APPLICATION = "config.wsgi.application"

TEMPLATES = [
    {
        "BACKEND": "django.template.backends.django.DjangoTemplates",
        "DIRS": [],
        "APP_DIRS": True,
        "OPTIONS": {"context_processors": []},
    }
]

DATABASES = {
    "default": {
        "ENGINE": "django.db.backends.postgresql",
        "NAME": env("DB_NAME", "fusion_integrated"),
        "USER": env("DB_USER", "fusion_admin"),
        "PASSWORD": env("DB_PASSWORD", ""),
        "HOST": env("DB_HOST", "127.0.0.1"),
        "PORT": env("DB_PORT", "5432"),

        "CONN_MAX_AGE": env_int("DB_CONN_MAX_AGE", 0),

}

IAM_BASE_URL = env("IAM_BASE_URL", "http://127.0.0.1:8001")
IAM_API_PREFIX = env("IAM_API_PREFIX", "/api")
IAM_SERVICE_TOKEN = env("IAM_SERVICE_TOKEN", "")
IAM_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = env_int("IAM_TIMEOUT_SECONDS", 5)
IAM_SESSION_CACHE_SECONDS = env_int("IAM_SESSION_CACHE_SECONDS", 60)
IAM_AUTH_COOKIE_NAME = env("IAM_AUTH_COOKIE_NAME", "fusion_session")

CACHES = {
    "default": (
        {
            "BACKEND": "django.core.cache.backends.redis.RedisCache",

        }
        if env("REDIS_CACHE_URL")
        else {
            "BACKEND": "django.core.cache.backends.locmem.LocMemCache",
            "LOCATION": "fusion-integrated",
        }
    )

CELERY_TASK_REJECT_ON_WORKER_LOST = True

                    "django.core.mail.backends.console.EmailBackend")

#: A dozen events a day is legitimate during a drive; thirty is a bug.
NOTIFY_DAILY_CAP_PER_RECIPIENT = env_int("NOTIFY_DAILY_CAP_PER_RECIPIENT", 20)

PLACEMENT_UPLOAD_ROOT = env(
    "PLACEMENT_UPLOAD_ROOT",
    str(Path.home() / ".local" / "share" / "fusion-integrated" / "uploads"))
#: When set, legacy reads go to nginx via X-Accel-Redirect. Must be `internal;`.
PLACEMENT_UPLOAD_INTERNAL_PREFIX = env("PLACEMENT_UPLOAD_INTERNAL_PREFIX", "")

# No multipart endpoints remain, so this only caps the JSON body.
DATA_UPLOAD_MAX_MEMORY_SIZE = 1024 * 1024

REST_FRAMEWORK = {
    "DEFAULT_AUTHENTICATION_CLASSES": [
        "fusion_auth.authentication.IamSessionAuthentication",
    ],
    "DEFAULT_PERMISSION_CLASSES": [
        "fusion_auth.permissions.IsAuthenticatedPrincipal",
    ],
    "DEFAULT_PAGINATION_CLASS": "core.api.pagination.CursorPagination",
    "PAGE_SIZE": 25,
    "DEFAULT_FILTER_BACKENDS": ["django_filters.rest_framework.DjangoFilterBackend"],
    "EXCEPTION_HANDLER": "core.api.exceptions.exception_handler",
    "DEFAULT_SCHEMA_CLASS": "drf_spectacular.openapi.AutoSchema",
    "UNAUTHENTICATED_USER": None,
    # Unset, DRF throttles on the whole client-controlled X-Forwarded-For.
    "NUM_PROXIES": env_int("DJANGO_NUM_PROXIES", 1),
    # Not DRF's ScopedRateThrottle: it keys on request.user.pk, absent here.
    "DEFAULT_THROTTLE_CLASSES": ["core.api.throttling.PrincipalScopedThrottle"],
    # Only endpoints opting in via `throttle_scope` are limited.
    "DEFAULT_THROTTLE_RATES": {
        "recruiter_login": "5/min",
        "recruiter_invite_accept": "10/hour",
        "apply": "30/hour",
        "export": "5/hour",
        "upload": "20/hour",
        "directory_search": "120/hour",
    },
}

# Recruiter passwords only; PBKDF2 verifies an older hash, then upgrades it.
PASSWORD_HASHERS = [
    "django.contrib.auth.hashers.Argon2PasswordHasher",
    "django.contrib.auth.hashers.PBKDF2PasswordHasher",
]

SPECTACULAR_SETTINGS = {
    "TITLE": "Fusion-Integrated API",
    "DESCRIPTION": "Non-academic platform. Independent modules, one login.",
    "VERSION": "1.0.0",
    "SERVE_INCLUDE_SCHEMA": False,
}

CORS_ALLOW_ALL_ORIGINS = False
CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS = env_list("DJANGO_CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS", ["http://localhost:5173"])
CORS_ALLOW_CREDENTIALS = True

LANGUAGE_CODE = "en-us"
TIME_ZONE = "Asia/Kolkata"
# After TIME_ZONE, which it reads, or a crontab entry fires at the wrong hour.
CELERY_TIMEZONE = TIME_ZONE
CELERY_ENABLE_UTC = True
USE_I18N = True
USE_TZ = True
STATIC_URL = "/static/"
STATIC_ROOT = BASE_DIR / "staticfiles"

SECURE_CONTENT_TYPE_NOSNIFF = True
SECURE_REFERRER_POLICY = "strict-origin-when-cross-origin"
# SAMEORIGIN, not DENY: Fusion-client embeds these screens, same origin in prod.
X_FRAME_OPTIONS = "SAMEORIGIN"

# W003: CSRF is enforced by core/api/csrf.py. See the note above MIDDLEWARE.

SILENCED_SYSTEM_CHECKS = ["security.W003", "security.W019"]

LOGGING = {

}

"""The authenticated actor.

Called `principal`, not `user`, deliberately: there is no Django user behind
it. It is a value object built from what IAM said, and it is what every
permission check reads.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass

from fusion_auth.client import IamSession


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Principal:
    user_id: int
    username: str
    display_name: str
    kind: str
    active_role: str | None
    roles: tuple[str, ...]
    permissions: frozenset[str]
    modules: tuple[str, ...]
    #: Built by the IAM so one sidebar can span every Fusion app.
    navigation: tuple[dict, ...] = ()
    email: str = ""

    # DRF pokes at these on request.user
    is_authenticated: bool = True
    is_anonymous: bool = False

    @classmethod
    def from_session(cls, s: IamSession) -> Principal:
        return cls(
            user_id=s.user_id, username=s.username, display_name=s.display_name,
            kind=s.kind, active_role=s.active_role, roles=s.roles,
            permissions=s.permissions, modules=s.modules, email=s.email,
            navigation=s.navigation,
        )

    def has_permission(self, code: str) -> bool:
        return code in self.permissions

    def has_any_permission(self, *codes: str) -> bool:
        return any(c in self.permissions for c in codes)

    def has_module(self, code: str) -> bool:
        return code in self.modules

    def __str__(self) -> str:
        return f"{self.username}({self.user_id})"

"""The module registry — what modules exist and where they live in the UI.

A module is a ROW here, not a boolean column keyed by a designation name as in
the legacy ModuleAccess table, so adding one is an insert rather than a schema
migration and renaming a role cannot silently break access. Who may enter is
IAM's decision and arrives in the token.
"""
from django.db import models

from core.db.mixins import TimeStampedModel


class Module(TimeStampedModel):
    STATUS = [("planned", "Planned"), ("active", "Active"),
              ("deprecated", "Deprecated")]

    code = models.CharField(max_length=48, unique=True)      # placement_cell
    label = models.CharField(max_length=80)                  # "Placement Cell"
    icon = models.CharField(max_length=48, default="FaCircle")
    base_path = models.CharField(max_length=80)              # /placement
    nav_section = models.CharField(max_length=48, default="Modules")
    sort_order = models.PositiveSmallIntegerField(default=100)
    status = models.CharField(max_length=16, choices=STATUS, default="planned")

    class Meta:
        db_table = "accesscontrol_module"
        ordering = ["nav_section", "sort_order", "label"]

    def __str__(self) -> str:
        return self.code


class NavItem(TimeStampedModel):
    """A link inside a module. Hidden unless the caller holds

## Goal
Implement an Employee Leave Management (ELM) module as an integrated component of the Fusion ERP system, leveraging existing authentication, role management, and UI patterns while adhering to ELM specifications.

## Constraints & Preferences
- Reuse Fusion ERP's IAM (Fusion_System_Administrator) for identity, RBAC, and user directory.
- Follow existing single-login shell architecture (no duplicate user tables).
- Do not rebuild common functionality (auth, logging, UI framework, DB schema patterns).
- Compliance with ELM specs (problem statement, functional requirements, workflows).
- Use Python 3.12, uv, and Docker as per setup instructions.
- Validate via `make check` CI pipeline.

## Progress
### Done
- [x] Confirmed Fusion-Integrated repo structure and authentication architecture (IAM-backed, two login types).
- [x] Identified ELM specification artifacts in `/Volumes/T7-Tools/fusion-qwen-elm/elm_specs/` (6 files: problem statement, functional requirements, etc.).
- [x] Verified reference module patterns (placement, directory modules) and project build workflow (`make install`, `make up`, `make dev`).
- [x] Read and analyzed ELM Problem Statement v1.4 (FINAL SYNCHRONIZED BASELINE) covering context, leave categories (CL, RH, SCL, EL, COL, VL), and entitlement rules.
- [x] Read and analyzed ELM Functional Requirements Specification v1.5 (32 Coherent CFRs, 128 Atomic FRs).
- [x] Read and analyzed ELM Use Case Specifications v1.4 (14+ use cases including Apply for Leave, Respond to Substitute Request, Review Leave-Related Request at Unit Head, etc.).

### In Progress
- [ ] Study reference modules (placement, directory) for code structure, DB schema patterns, and integration points.
- [ ] Begin implementing ELM data models, APIs, and UI components aligned with Fusion backend/frontend patterns.

### Blocked
- [ ] None (spec files read; ready for implementation)

## Key Decisions
- **IAM Integration**: Use Fusion_System_Administrator for identity/RBAC (no local user table).
- **Single Login**: ELM module shares Fusion's shell login; operators use `/sysadmin/` console.
- **Reference Modules**: placement and directory guide backend/frontend structure and DB patterns.
- **Leave Categories**: Support CL (8 days/year), RH (2 days/year), SCL (up to 15 days/year), EL, COL, VL within same application process.
- **Sanctioning Flow**: Unit Head reviews/recommends → Higher-sanction path → Final decision by Sanctioning Authority (Deputy Registrar, Dean, Registrar, Director, etc.)

## Next Steps
1. Analyze reference modules (placement, directory) for integration patterns (DB, auth, UI).
2. Draft ELM data models, API routes, and UI components using Fusion's core structure.
3. Implement leave entitlement tracking, application workflows, and sanctioning decision processes.
4. Validate via `make check` and CI pipeline after implementation.

## Critical Context
- **No User Table**: ELM uses Fusion's IAM for identity; all user data (students/faculty/staff) comes from Fusion_System_Administrator.
- **Two Login Paths**: Users (ELM module) and operators (sysadmin console) have separate logins but share IAM backend.
- **Build Workflow**: `make install` sets up uv venv; `make up` spins PostgreSQL + Redis; `make dev` starts app.
- **Spec Files**: ELM specs partitioned into 33 parts (functional requirements) and 3 parts (problem statement).
- **Use Cases**: 14 primary use cases identified including leave applications, substitutions, unit head reviews, higher-sanction routing, and resumption of duty.
- **Traceability**: 32 Coherent CFRs map to 128 Atomic FRs with traceability to 107 historical SRS-EL baseline items.

# Fusion-Integrated

The non-academic platform. **Placement Cell** first; more modules later.
**Independent modules, one login.**

This service holds **no user table**. Identity, RBAC and common directory data
(student info, faculty info, staff info) all come from

# Fusion-Integrated

The non-academic platform. **Placement Cell** first; more modules later.
**Independent modules, one login.**

This service holds **no user table**. Identity, RBAC and common directory data
(student info, faculty info, staff info) all come from
**Fusion_System_Administrator**, which is the IAM.

```
        Fusion_System_Administrator   ( = the IAM )
        owns fusion_system_db
        · identity  — authenticates ALL users
        · RBAC      — roles, permissions, module grants
        · directory — student / faculty / staff info
        · its OWN console at /sysadmin/, its own operator login
                 │
                 │  HTTP   /api/iam/v1/*
                 ▼
        Fusion-Integrated                ← this repo
        owns fusion_integrated
        backend  →  placement  (more modules later)
        client   →  the shell: one login, one sidebar
        holds only user_id references — no user table
```

## Two logins, on purpose

|  | Who | Where | Against |
|---|---|---|---|
| **User login** | students, faculty, staff | this app's shell | the ERP user pool, via IAM |
| **Operator login** | sysadmin operators | `/sysadmin/`, its own URL | the console's own account pool |

Users get **one** login for every module they are granted. Operators keep a
separate door to the admin console — different audience, different account set.
Both are backed by the same identity service; they are not the same login page.

---

## Quick start

```bash
make install          # uv venv + dependencies
make up               # postgres + 2× redis (cache and broker, separately)
cp .env.example .env
make migrate seed     # schema, module registry, demo data
make dev              # http://127.0.0.1:8002
make check            # everything CI runs
```

Requires Python 3.12, [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) and Docker.

---

## What "independent module" actually means here

Not a naming convention — four rules, each enforced by a CI job that has been
tested against a deliberate violation:

| Rule | Enforced by |
|---|---|
| A module may reach another **only** through its `contracts.py` | `lint-imports` |
| **No foreign key crosses a module boundary** | `ops/checks/no_cross_module_fk.py` |
| `domain/` may not import Django, DRF or Celery | `lint-imports` |
| Cross-module getters are **plural** — they take a sequence of ids | `ops/checks/contracts_are_plural.py` |

The payoff is concrete: every module owns its own tables and its own migration
file, so lifting one out into its own service later means changing one file's
implementation, not doing schema surgery.

The plural rule is the sneaky-useful one. There is no `get_employment(user_id)`
anywhere, only `get_employments(user_ids)` — which makes the N+1 not merely
discouraged but *unwritable*.

### Anatomy of a module

```
modules/placement/
├── apps.py          Django app config
├── registry.py      its sidebar entry — seeded by `manage.py seed_modules`
├── contracts.py     THE ONLY thing other modules may import
├── models.py        its own tables, its own migrations
├── domain/          pure Python. rules, state machine. no Django.
├── selectors/       all reads.  ownership filtering lives here
├── services/        all writes. transactions, audit rows, domain→HTTP translation
├── api/             thin: serializers, views, urls
└── tests/
```

Adding a module: create the directory, add one line to `DOMAIN_MODULES` in
`config/settings/base.py`, write `registry.py`, run `make seed`. Nothing central
to edit — no menu array, no boolean column, no shadow model.

---

## How a request is authorized

Two gates, both server-side, on **every** request:

```python
permission_classes = [
    HasModuleGrant("placement_cell"),               # is this module yours at all?
    HasPermission("placement_cell.application.view"),  # may you do this?
]
```

Both must pass; the default is deny. `fusion_auth` resolves the caller's session
against IAM (cookie or `Authorization: Token`), builds a `Principal`, and every
check reads that.

**The sidebar is server-driven.** `GET /api/v1/me` returns `navigation` already
filtered and already in render shape — the client does zero filtering, so it
cannot draw a module the server did not send. This replaces the legacy pattern
of a hardcoded client array whose ids had to exactly match database *column*
names.

Ownership is enforced by filtering the queryset in the selector, never by
fetching-then-checking, which is why a foreign id naturally yields **404** and
not 403 (403 would leak existence and turn any id column into an enumeration
oracle).

---

## Layout

```
config/          settings (base/dev/test/prod), urls, celery
core/            shared kernel — error envelope, pagination, request-id, mixins
fusion_auth/     the IAM client, Principal, authentication, the two permission gates
modules/
  directory/     local projection of IAM's user data (a cache with a table)
  accesscontrol/ module registry + the server-driven sidebar
  placement/     companies, postings, applications, eligibility, state machine
ops/checks/      the boundary enforcement scripts
client/          the shell — Vite + React 18 + TS + Mantine 7.13
```

`core/` may not import `modules` — it is a leaf, and CI checks that too.

---

## Testing

```bash
make test          # 40 tests, ~0.6s
```

Domain tests are pure Python with no database, which is why they run in
milliseconds — that is the whole point of the no-Django-in-`domain/` rule. The
IAM is never contacted: `conftest.py` swaps in an in-memory fake, so the suite
needs no network and no running Fusion_System_Administrator.

---

## The client

```bash
cd client && npm install && npm run dev      # :5173, proxies /api to :8002
```

Vite + React 18 + TypeScript (strict) + Mantine **7.13.4, pinned to match the
sysadmin client** so the two apps look like one product. `theme.ts` and
`AppShellLayout.module.css` are ports of that client's files, not a redesign.

Routes are built **only** for modules the server granted, so an ungranted module
has no route — deep-linking it hits NotFound rather than an empty shell. Module
pages are lazy chunks (`PostingsPage`, `ApplicationsPage` build separately).

## Extracting a module into its own repo

This is what "independent" is for. Removing `hr` and `leave` from this codebase
touched **five files**, none of them in `placement`:

```
config/settings/base.py     one line in DOMAIN_MODULES
config/urls.py              one include()
devtools/…/seed_demo.py     fixtures
.importlinter               contract membership
modules/<name>/             the directory itself
```

Nothing in `placement`, `directory`, `accesscontrol`, `core` or `fusion_auth`
referenced them, because the boundary rules make that impossible. The same holds
in reverse: lifting a module into a separate repo means taking its directory and
its migrations, then replacing its `contracts.py` callers with HTTP.

## Status

Working today: the module system, both authorization gates, the server-driven
sidebar, the directory projection, the placement application state machine with
an append-only audit trail, and the client shell with login.

**Blocking next step — the IAM side.** `Fusion_System_Administrator` currently
authenticates operators only; its own router says so: *"this is what makes admin
operators a separate account set from the 3277 managed ERP users."* It needs
ERP-user authentication plus `/api/iam/v1/{auth/login, auth/logout, me,
directory/users}`. The client for those is written and tested against a fake —
the expected contract is in `fusion_auth/client.py`.

Then: offers and selection rounds, the declared-CPI integration.

Design documents — architecture, ADRs, the RBAC model, the placement domain and
the academic-snapshot contract — are in [`docs/`](docs/).
